result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=with, B=without): Both slides show all six figures correctly and openly show the +650% Fennmark rise and the -80% Tallgrass drop. B has a shorter headline that reads faster, larger change figures, and it flags that the Fennmark increase needs a customer plan. A states the trade-off and the revenue drop honestly, but its headline wraps to two lines and its side-panel text is small; neither slide proposes a floor. | pass 2 (A=without, B=with): Both slides show all six bills correctly, and both state the net change for the three customers ($560 to $435). A is easier to take in at a glance: a short one-line headline, large percentage changes, and one clear decision box. Its note says Fennmark's increase needs a customer plan. B spells out the trade-off and the revenue drop more fully, but its two-line headline, dense side panel and very small footnote make it harder to read at slide size. Neither slide sets a price floor.
